diagnostic_evidence.quote: In both cases, the solution of the augmented Lagrangian formulation coincides with the solution of the discrete problem~\eqref{eq:discrete-problem}.
If $\Gamma_p \neq \emptyset$, the discrete solution $u_h$ satisfies $\dv{u_h} = -\piqst(g)$ on $\Omega_h$.
since the additional terms vanish for the solution of the discrete problem~\eqref{eq:discrete-problem}.

issues.failure_explanation: For mixed boundary conditions ($\Gamma_p\neq\emptyset$), Lemma~\ref{lem:mass-conservation} already gives exact discrete conservation $\dv{u_h}=-\pi_h^0(g)$. The augmented terms are built so that they vanish on that same solution, so the augmented formulation cannot change the discrete conservation law in the mixed case; it can at most affect solver-level enforcement.

failure_location.quote: which may be used to design effective preconditioners and to better preserve mass conservation in the case of mixed boundary conditions.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Rephrase the claim: in mixed boundary conditions conservation is already exact by Lemma~\ref{lem:mass-conservation}; the augmented formulation is for preconditioning/solver control, while in the pure-flux case it controls the otherwise undetermined constant mode.
issues.overall_effect: The introductory claim that the augmented Lagrangian variant better preserves mass conservation for mixed boundary conditions is misleading. No theorem is invalidated; the inaccurate scope is about the practical role of the augmented terms.
issues.title: Augmented Lagrangian advertised as improving mixed-BC mass conservation
issues.why_classification: This is a wording/scope correction only; the exact conservation statement and the algebraic identity used for the augmented form remain intact.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: where in the last inequality we used the properties of $v$, the trace inequality \eqref{eq:cut-trace} and the local interpolation estimate for $\Iv$

The interpolation estimates for $u$, $\dv{u}$ and $p$, together with the trace inequality for the boundary term in $\|\cdot\|_{\mathrm{d},h}$ and Assumption~\ref{as:extensions}, then prove the theorem.

issues.failure_explanation: The stability proof bounds the unfitted-boundary trace of the $H(\mathrm{div})$ interpolation error through a cut-cell estimate containing $\|\nabla(v-\Iv v)\\|_{L^2(T)}$, and the error proof later uses the same kind of boundary-interpolation control for the penalty part of $\|u-u_h\|_{\mathrm{d},h}$. Assumption~\ref{as:discrete-spaces} supplies only $L^2$ interpolation and divergence commutativity; an $H(\mathrm{div})$-conforming interpolator is not assumed to be an $H^1$-approximant. The mixed/flux-boundary inf-sup and the stated optimal strong-norm flux estimate are therefore not justified as written.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: For stability, replace the gradient trace step by the standard $H(\mathrm{div})$ trace inequality $\|w\cdot n\|_{L^2(\partial T)}^2\lesssim h^{-1}\|w\|_{L^2(T)}^2+h\|\dv w\|_{L^2(T)}^2$, using $\dv{\Iv v}=\Iv\dv v$; in the stability construction $\dv(v-\Iv v)=0$. For the a priori theorem, either add an explicit cut-boundary supercloseness hypothesis for $\Iv$ or state the flux estimate in $L^2(\Omega_h)$ with divergence and pressure bounds rather than in the penalty norm.
issues.overall_effect: The uniform inf-sup argument for mixed or flux boundary conditions and the optimal error bound in the penalty norm $\|\cdot\|_{\mathrm{d},h}$ are unproven unless an $H(\mathrm{div})$ trace/supercloseness argument or an additional hypothesis is supplied. The $L^2$/pressure conclusions can survive only after weakening the flux norm or adding a nontrivial boundary-approximation hypothesis.
issues.title: H(div) interpolant used as if it had H1 boundary interpolation control
issues.why_classification: The stability repair is local, but the advertised optimal rate in the penalty norm does not follow from the stated assumptions; preserving it needs an added supercloseness hypothesis, while the supported comparable version weakens the flux norm. This is more than a typo yet avoids rebuilding the whole analysis.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: The operator $\extv$ is a \emph{non-conforming} discrete extension operator; its image is not a subspace of $H(\mathrm{div},\Omega)$.

issues.failure_explanation: As written, $\Vh^-$ consists of $H(\mathrm{div},\Omega_h^{\mathrm{in}})$ functions whose restrictions to every aggregate $T\in\mathcal{T}_h^{\mathrm{ag}}$ lie in $\mathcal{V}(T)$. Non-trivial aggregates contain cut cells outside $\Omega_h^{\mathrm{in}}$, so the restriction condition is not defined for functions whose domain is only $\Omega_h^{\mathrm{in}}$; moreover a space on $\Omega_h^{\mathrm{in}}$ cannot have discontinuous normal components on $\mathcal{F}_h^{\mathrm{cut}}$ as stated. Thus $\extv:\Vh\to\Vh^-$ and the cell-wise term with $\Hv=\extv$ are not well-defined on $\Omega_h^{\mathrm{cut}}$ as written.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Define the codomain as the broken space on the active mesh/aggregates: locally $\mathcal{V}(T)$ on every aggregate, with $H(\mathrm{div})$ normal continuity only on facets away from $\mathcal{F}_h^{\mathrm{cut}}$ and no normal-continuity requirement across $\mathcal{F}_h^{\mathrm{cut}}$.
issues.overall_effect: The extension-based choice in the cell-wise stabilisation lemma is not defined by the stated codomain; the aggregate-wise projection choice used in the bulk numerical method is not the one affected. Main theorems remain conditional on the stabilisation assumptions.
issues.title: Extension operator codomain is not a well-defined superspace
issues.why_classification: The prose construction already gives the aggregate-wise repair, and the projection variant used numerically is unaffected; no main rate or regime is lost.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: To validate the method, we utilise the following manufactured exact solutions.

issues.failure_explanation: On $\Gamma^{\mathrm{int}}$, with the radial normal and $[p]=p_2-p_1$, the manufactured fields give $[p]=-1$ and $\eta_{\mathrm{int}}\{u\cdot n\}=-1$, so the first transmission condition is consistent. But $\{p\}=\sin(r_{\mathrm{int}}^2)+3/2$, whereas the stated $\hat p$ gives $\hat p+\frac{\eta_{\mathrm{int}}}{8}[u\cdot n]=\hat p-\frac{1}{4(4\cos(r_{\mathrm{int}}^2)+3)}$; at $r_{\mathrm{int}}=0.3$ this is about $1.5899$ versus $2.4988$. The opposite jump convention changes the second value to about $2.5704$, still not equality. Algebraically, the stated $\hat p$ would require the sine terms in its numerator to be multiplied by $r_{\mathrm{int}}^2$.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace $\hat p$ by the value forced by the transmission conditions, equivalently $\sin(r_{\mathrm{int}}^2)+3/2+\frac{1}{4(4\cos(r_{\mathrm{int}}^2)+3)}$ up to the chosen jump sign, and regenerate the interface results; or change the parameters to the consistent case for which the copied $\hat p$ holds.
issues.overall_effect: The interface experiment is not a validation of the stated transmission problem as written, so Figure~\ref{fig:interface.example} and Table~\ref{tab:Linftydiverrors.interface} are unreliable until the data are corrected and recomputed. The analytical stability/error theory is unaffected.
issues.title: Interface manufactured solution does not satisfy the stated transmission data
issues.why_classification: The mathematical correction is a contained formula repair, but the advertised numerical validation and its tables/figures must be redone; the formal theory does not supply the missing consistent data.
